Commercial Bank of Ceylon PLC (COMB), Sri Lanka's largest private-sector bank, a licensed commercial bank (FYE 31 December). FIRST financial_statements entry for this symbol -- no prior rows existed. Filing is the Interim Financial Statements for the six months ended 30 June 2026 (H1 2026), source_id '52504', confirmed against the live CSE API as the Bank's latest filing. This entry uses the filing's 6-MONTH CUMULATIVE (H1) columns, not the quarter-only columns also shown, consistent with other bank entries this session. Group income statement is on PDF page 5; the separate Bank (Company, standalone) income statement is on PDF page 7 -- both are (Audited), per the filing's own labelling and the CFO/Chairman/MD certification on page 10. Balance sheet (Statement of Financial Position, Group and Bank columns side by side) spans PDF pages 9-10; cash flow statement (Group and Bank columns side by side) is on PDF page 13. Mapped per bank convention: revenue = 'Total operating income'; operating_profit = 'Operating profit before taxes on financial services', the Bank's own subtotal (Group: Rs.63,616,433k vs Rs.55,588,974k, +14.44%; Bank: Rs.61,290,161k vs Rs.53,940,938k, +13.62%). 'Taxes on financial services' (Group Rs.10,562,933k, +20.38%; Bank Rs.10,440,075k, +20.03%) is not a separate stored field -- profit_before_tax stored here is AFTER this levy, matching the filing's own 'Profit before income tax' line (Group) / 'Profit before income tax' line (Bank). finance_costs/finance_income left blank -- interest expense (Rs.91,955,070k Group) is already netted into revenue via Net Interest Income. current_assets/current_liabilities/inventory/trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank per bank convention. short_term_borrowings = 'Due to banks' + 'Securities sold under repurchase agreements' (both short-tenor interbank/money-market funding): Group 56,336,233 + 105,150,776 = 161,487,009; Bank 35,257,486 + 106,821,588 = 142,079,074. long_term_borrowings = 'Financial liabilities at amortised cost - other borrowings' + 'Subordinated liabilities' (debentures/green bonds, per the separate 'INFORMATION ON DEBENTURES AND GREEN BONDS' note on PDF page 25 showing Total-Bank Rs.69,129,830k / Total-Group Rs.70,383,784k of subordinated debt, consistent with the subordinated-liabilities balance sheet line): Group 21,555,179 + 75,531,398 = 97,086,577; Bank 21,555,179 + 74,195,272 = 95,750,451. 'Financial liabilities at amortised cost - due to depositors' (Group Rs.3,015,155,478k / Bank Rs.2,908,185,047k) is deliberately EXCLUDED from both borrowings fields -- deposit funding, not debt. Balance-sheet identities tie out exactly: Group Total Assets 3,739,565,733 = Total Liabilities 3,375,676,828 + Total Equity 363,888,905; Bank Total Assets 3,592,606,230 = Total Liabilities 3,244,732,534 + Total Equity 347,873,696. Income-statement identities tie out exactly: Group PBT 53,053,500 - tax 17,630,446 = PAT 35,423,054; Bank PBT 50,850,086 - tax 17,056,752 = PAT 33,793,334. minority_interest (Group only, Rs.494,453k) = profit attributable to non-controlling interest; the Bank/Company row is a single entity with no NCI so that field is omitted there. capex = Purchase of property, plant and equipment + Purchase of intangible assets (proceeds from disposals not netted out, consistent with NTB/CBNK convention this session): Group 2,147,873 + 1,090,870 = 3,238,743; Bank 1,656,536 + 1,034,223 = 2,690,759. shares_in_issue = Voting (1,556,228,193) + Non-Voting (97,325,945) = 1,653,554,138 as at 30 June 2026, per the 'INFORMATION ON ORDINARY SHARES OF THE BANK' note on PDF page 23 -- same combined share register applies to both the Group and Bank rows. Cross-checked against EPS: Group profit attributable to equity holders of the Bank (34,928,601k) / basic EPS (21.14) implies ~1,652,533,806 weighted-average shares, within 0.06% of the disclosed period-end count of 1,653,554,138 -- the small gap is expected (weighted-average vs period-end count, given new shares were issued during the period via the FY2025 final scrip dividend, per the Statement of Changes in Equity on PDF page 11: 3,479,200k of stated capital added 'satisfied in the form of issue and allotment of new shares'). Bank-basis PAT (33,793,334k) / EPS (20.45) implies ~1,652,529,003 shares, similarly within 0.06%. No column-swap issues found -- Group and Bank subtotals, and six-month vs quarter columns, all reconcile internally and against the page-2-to-4 press-release narrative (e.g. Bank PBT +12.39% to Rs.50.85bn and PAT +12.45% to Rs.33.79bn per the press release match the page-7 table's Rs.50,850,086k/+12.39% and Rs.33,793,334k/+12.45% exactly).

interim_updates.note_text: Commercial Bank of Ceylon Group's H1 2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026) results show broad-based growth across the balance sheet and income statement, not a one-off or tax-driven swing. Deposits crossed the Rs.3 trillion threshold for the first time among private banks, growing Rs.315.13bn in the six months to Rs.3.02tn; the gross loan book grew Rs.270.43bn to Rs.2.36tn. Group gross income rose 18.28% to Rs.209.16bn and interest income rose 17.05% to Rs.171.65bn, driving net interest income +15.81% to Rs.79.69bn. Total Operating Income (this entry's 'revenue') grew 17.85% to Rs.109.07bn. Impairment charges and other losses rose a sharper 33.44% to Rs.14.85bn -- but management explicitly frames this as a PRUDENTIAL BUILD-UP, not a sign of deteriorating credit quality: 'in the backdrop of uncertainties in the geopolitical environment.' This framing is corroborated by the Bank's own asset-quality ratios, which actually IMPROVED over the same period -- net Stage 3 (impaired loans) to total loans fell to 1.38% from 1.54% at end-2025, gross Stage 3 ratio fell to 5.32% from 5.81%, and the Impairment (Stage 3) to Stage 3 loans coverage ratio rose to 74.14% from 73.50%. Operating expenses grew 18.47% to Rs.30.61bn as staff strength crossed 6,000 in June 2026, yet the Cost-to-Income Ratio (excluding taxes on financial services) still IMPROVED to 27.82% from 29.66% a year earlier, since revenue growth outpaced cost growth. Net Interest Margin held flat at 4.51% (annualised), unchanged from end-2025. Group operating profit before taxes on financial services grew 14.44% to Rs.63.62bn, and after a 20.38% rise in taxes on financial services (Rs.10.56bn), Group profit before income tax grew 13.33% to Rs.53.05bn. Income tax expense rose 12.67% to Rs.17.63bn (Rs.15.65bn prior year) -- a normal, roughly proportional increase with no unusual credit or swing -- so Group profit after tax growth of 13.66% (to Rs.35.42bn) tracks PBT growth (13.33%) closely, confirming the earnings growth is genuine operating performance rather than a tax-line artefact. Standalone Bank (Company) PBT grew 12.39% to Rs.50.85bn and PAT grew 12.45% to Rs.33.79bn, both consistent with the Group trend. Return on Equity (Bank) improved to 20.28% from 19.51% at end-2025; Return on Assets before tax rose to 2.99% from 2.96%. Capital and liquidity remain comfortably above regulatory minimums: Tier 1 Capital Ratio 13.23% (min 10%), Total Capital Ratio 16.58% (min 14%), Rupee liquidity coverage ratio 444.92% and all-currency 253.94% (both against a 100% minimum).

interim_updates.takeaway: COMB's H1 2026 growth is genuinely broad-based operating performance -- deposits past Rs.3tn, loan book +Rs.270.43bn, Total Operating Income +17.85%, operating profit +14.44%, PBT +13.33% (Group) / +12.39% (Bank) -- with PAT growth (13.66% Group / 12.45% Bank) tracking PBT growth closely and no unusual tax-line swing distorting the headline (unlike other banks entered this session where a tax credit or one-off item inflated PAT growth well beyond PBT growth). The one line that grew faster than revenue -- impairment charges, +33.44% to Rs.14.85bn -- is explicitly a prudential, forward-looking provision against geopolitical/macro uncertainty rather than a symptom of credit deterioration: Stage 3 (impaired loan) ratios actually improved over the same period, both gross (5.32% vs 5.81%) and net (1.38% vs 1.54%).

operational_highlights: Group deposits crossed Rs.3 trillion for the first time (+Rs.315.13bn in 6 months to Rs.3.02tn); gross loan book +Rs.270.43bn to Rs.2.36tn; Total Assets +Rs.361bn (10.68%) since December 2025 to Rs.3.74tn
Group gross income +18.28% YoY to Rs.209.16bn; interest income +17.05% to Rs.171.65bn; Net Interest Income +15.81% to Rs.79.69bn; Total Operating Income +17.85% to Rs.109.07bn

Impairment charges and other losses +33.44% YoY to Rs.14.85bn -- explicitly described by management as a prudential measure against geopolitical/macro uncertainty, NOT credit deterioration: net Stage 3 (impaired loans) to total loans ratio actually improved to 1.38% from 1.54% at end-2025, and gross Stage 3 ratio improved to 5.32% from 5.81%

Operating expenses +18.47% to Rs.30.61bn as staff strength crossed 6,000 in June 2026; Cost-to-Income Ratio (ex taxes on financial services) still improved to 27.82% from 29.66%, as revenue growth outpaced cost growth

Group operating profit before taxes on financial services +14.44% to Rs.63.62bn; Group PBT +13.33% to Rs.53.05bn; Group PAT +13.66% to Rs.35.42bn -- PAT growth tracks PBT growth closely (income tax expense rose a proportional 12.67% to Rs.17.63bn, no unusual swing)

Standalone Bank (Company) PBT +12.39% to Rs.50.85bn; PAT +12.45% to Rs.33.79bn -- consistent with the Group trend, confirming genuine operating strength rather than subsidiary-driven or one-off effects

Net Interest Margin flat at 4.51% (annualised), unchanged from end-2025; Bank Return on Equity improved to 20.28% from 19.51%; Tier 1 Capital Ratio 13.23% and Total Capital Ratio 16.58%, both comfortably above the 10%/14% regulatory minimums
key_drivers: Deposit growth past the Rs.3tn threshold (+Rs.315.13bn in 6 months) and loan book growth (+Rs.270.43bn) are the primary volume drivers behind the 15.81% Net Interest Income growth to Rs.79.69bn

The 33.44% rise in impairment charges (to Rs.14.85bn) is a prudential, forward-looking provision build-up tied to geopolitical/macro uncertainty per management's own explanation -- not deteriorating asset quality, since Stage 3 (impaired loan) ratios improved over the same period (net 1.38% vs 1.54%, gross 5.32% vs 5.81%)

Operating expense growth (+18.47% to Rs.30.61bn, staff strength past 6,000) did not erode profitability -- Cost-to-Income Ratio (ex FS taxes) improved to 27.82% from 29.66%, showing revenue growth (Total Operating Income +17.85%) comfortably outpaced cost growth

Income tax expense rose a roughly proportional 12.67% (Rs.15.65bn to Rs.17.63bn), so unlike some peer banks this period, PAT growth (13.66% Group) closely tracks PBT growth (13.33% Group) with no material tax-line distortion of the headline
